PHASE 107 IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: Agent Queue REST Endpoints + WebSocket + Startup Integration

## Summary
Exposed agent queue methods through REST API, added WebSocket for real-time queue monitoring, and integrated TTL manager + scheduled retention + auto-recovery into the container startup event. Addresses GPT-4o Phase 106 findings: Medium (agent queue not exposed via REST, no WebSocket, hardcoded TTL).

## Components Built

### 1. Agent Queue REST Endpoints (6 new endpoints)
- POST /agent/submit: submit an agent task via AgentQueueIntegrator
- POST /agent/execute: submit and wait for task completion (synchronous-style)
- GET /agent/task/{task_id}: get agent task status
- GET /agent/tasks: list agent tasks (filterable by agent_id, status, limit)
- GET /agent/stats: combined queue + DLQ statistics
- POST /agent/dlq/{task_id}/requeue: re-queue a failed agent task from DLQ

### 2. WebSocket Real-Time Monitoring
- GET /ws: WebSocket endpoint for real-time queue monitoring
- WebSocketManager class: connect, disconnect, broadcast, periodic broadcast
- Periodic broadcast: sends queue stats + DLQ stats every 5 seconds to all connected clients
- Initial state sent on connection
- Ping/pong support for keepalive
- Connection count tracked in health endpoint (ws_connections)
- Dead connections automatically cleaned up

### 3. TTL Configuration Endpoints
- GET /ttl/config: get current TTL seconds and cleanup interval
- POST /ttl/config: set TTL seconds and cleanup interval (runtime configurable)

### 4. Startup Integration
All subsystems now initialized on container startup:
- PostgreSQL pool initialization (3 retries, 2s delay)
- Persistence callback set on execution_queue
- Auto-recovery of pending tasks from PG
- TTL manager periodic cleanup started (3600s interval)
- Scheduled retention started (daily PG cleanup)
- WebSocket broadcast started (5s interval)

### 5. Shutdown Integration
All subsystems gracefully stopped:
- WebSocket broadcast stopped
- TTL periodic cleanup stopped
- Scheduled retention stopped
- Execution queue stopped
- PG pool closed

### 6. Tests (test_queue_api_v3.py, 16 tests)
TestAgentEndpoints (7): submit, task_status, not_found, list_tasks, list_filtered, stats, dlq_requeue_not_found
TestTTLConfig (2): get_ttl_config, set_ttl_config
TestHealthV3 (1): health with version 3.0.0, pg_connected, ttl_seconds, ws_connections
TestDLQEndpoints (4): stats, list, alert_config, set_alert_config
TestWebSocket (2): ws_manager_init, broadcast_empty

## Test Results
- 559 passed, 7 skipped (v3.0 replaces v2.0 tests: 16 vs 23, net -7)
- Total unique tests: 559 (all passing)
- 24 Docker containers running
- Queue API v3.0 live at https://evolvixos.com/queue/
- pg_connected: true, ttl_seconds: 86400, ws_connections: 0

## Key Achievements
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 106 Medium: Agent queue exposed via REST ✓
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 106 Medium: WebSocket support ✓
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 106 Medium: Configurable TTL ✓
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 106 Low: Startup integration ✓
- Full lifecycle: startup (PG, TTL, retention, WS, recovery) → shutdown (graceful stop all)
- 6 new agent REST endpoints + WebSocket endpoint
- Runtime-configurable TTL

## Known Limitations
- DLQ alerting webhook not tested end-to-end
- Real execution tests still skipped (need API keys)
- WebSocket not tested with actual client connection (only unit tests)
- No per-task TTL override
- Agent execute endpoint blocks until completion (not truly async via REST)
- No WebSocket authentication

## Questions for GPT-4o
1. Should we add WebSocket authentication (token-based)?
2. Should we add a non-blocking agent execute endpoint (returns task_id, poll for result)?
3. What should be the next priority: real execution tests with API keys, OS-level network isolation, or per-task TTL?
4. Should we integrate the queue with the existing agent_api.py (replace synchronous execution in agent framework)?
